subject: english-literature
title: A Christmas Carol Context Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch your thinking: was Dickens's novella a sermon, a protest, or a marketable ghost story?
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — essay-level analysis of A Christmas Carol's social and political context.
final_note: You weighed up Dickens as moralist, political reformer and storyteller — and how context shaped genre choices.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Dickens originally planned a pamphlet titled 'An Appeal to the People of England on behalf of the Poor Man's Child.'

He decided fiction would persuade more readers than a polemic. The Carol is essentially an argument dressed as a ghost story.

Scrooge is not just a miser — he voices laissez-faire economics and Malthusian ethics.

His transformation is therefore the transformation of an entire ideology. Dickens suggests Victorian Britain itself must wake up like Scrooge does.

Christmas in 1843 was being 'revived' — Prince Albert popularised trees; the first Christmas card was sent that year.

Dickens harnessed this revival to push Christian charity: Christmas should be the season the rich remember the poor. The novella helped invent the modern English Christmas.
